tone_statements.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2011. Demonstrative and relative constructions in Juu: a diachronic perspective. Handout, workshop 'Genealogical and Areal Relations in the Kalahari Basin', ICHL20, Osaka, 29 July 2011, 12 pp. [published version: Lionnet, Florian. 2014. Demonstrative and relative constructions in Ju: a diachronic account. In Tom Güldemann & Anne-Maria Fehn (eds.), Beyond 'Khoisan': Historical Relations in the Kalahari Basin (CILT 330), 181-207. Amsterdam: Benjamins. doi:10.1075/cilt.330.07lio]
tone_statements.quote: (19) Tentative reconstructions of Proto-Juu forms: (tones are not reconstructed8) ... [endnote 13:] The exact nature and origin of the extra-L tone in Juu languages, and the relation between the extra-L tone and depressor consonants or vowel colorings (breathy voice and pharyngealization in particular) is not well documented yet, but there seems to be a relation (if not systematic, at least very frequently attested) between extra-L tones and depressors in Juu.
tone_statements.locator: handout p.5 ex.(19) and p.12 endnote 13 (to p.8 (33b) 'super-L tone > L tone')
tone_statements.summary: Presupposes lexical tone in the Juu lects incl. NC !Xun, with at least L and an extra-low ('super-L') level distinguished in the transcription; extra-L tones said to correlate frequently with depressors (breathy voice, pharyngealization); no count of tones, no contour/TBU/downstep or stress statement; Proto-Juu tones explicitly not reconstructed.

sources.citation: WALS Online (Dryer & Haspelmath eds. 2013), language '!Xun (Ekoka)' [wals code xun, glottocode kung1261], source König & Heine 2001.
sources.note: No values coded for 13A (tone) or 14A-17A (stress) for this language.

sources.citation: Vedder, H. 1910. Grundriß einer Grammatik der Buschmannsprache vom Stamm der !Kû-Buschmänner. Zeitschrift für Kolonialsprachen 1: 5-24, 106-117.
sources.note: p.13-15 'Die Töne': five 'musikalische Töne' on monosyllables plus 'dynamische Töne'; p.15 verbatim (checked on page scan vedder_pages/): 'Für die zweisilbigen Worte gilt folgende Regel: Der Stärkeakzent liegt entweder auf der ersten Silbe !gụru donnern, oder auf der zweiten Silbe, !gurụ Nagel an Fingern und Zehen, oder er liegt auf beiden Silben gleichmäßig, !gụrụ Köcher. Die gleichmäßige Verteilung des Akzentes auf beide Silben wird leicht als Hochton wahrgenommen. Es ist indes nicht ausgeschlossen, daß auch einige zweisilbige Worte einen musikalischen Ton besitzen.' i.e. lexically contrast…

sources.citation: Takada, Akira. 2024. Doing being senior/junior: reconsidering naming and kinship relationships among the !Xun of north-central Namibia. Nordic Journal of African Studies 33(4): 406-416.
sources.note: Anthropology; identifies Ekoka !Xun as W2; uses König & Heine 2008 orthography 'tonal information omitted'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pratchett, Lee J. 2022. When verbs 'stay go' together: pseudo-coordination in Ju|'hoan and !Xun. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics Plus 65: 191-216.
sources.note: Syntax; Ekoka !Xun examples quoted from Heine & König 2015 / König & Heine 2001 with tone marks; mentions floating high tones; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Miller, Amanda. 2013. Northern Khoesan [phonetics and phonology]. In Rainer Vossen (ed.), The Khoesan Languages, 45-51. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Ju|'hoan-centred; mentions Ekoka !Xun and Mangetti Dune !Xung only for click types and the Back Vowel Constraint; notes for 'Okongo !Xung there exist a 1,200-wordlist and a basic grammar'. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Heine, Bernd & Henry Honken. 2010. The Kx'a family: a new Khoisan genealogy. Journal of Asian and African Studies (Tokyo) 79: 5-36.
sources.note: Comparative-historical (Proto-Kx'a). Takes W2 (Ekoka) as representative of NW-!Xun, W1 from Heikkinen. §2.1/2.5: 'most !Xun dialects distinguish four tone levels.. In both branches there is a tone system characterized by four distinct tone levels (Honken 2004).. a tonal analysis still needs to be done.' Nothing on stress/accent. Table 2 gives Heine & König's dialect classification (C1 Gaub, C2 Neitsas = Central branch).

sources.citation: Miller, Amanda. 2010. A prosodic account of Ju|'hoansi consonant distributional asymmetries. In M. Brenzinger & C. König (eds.), Khoisan Languages and Linguistics: Proceedings of the 1st International Symposium (Riezlern 2003), 53ff. Köln: Köppe.
sources.note: Cites Heine & König (2001:21) on Ekoka root-medial consonants and explicitly says 'the word prosody of Ekoka !Xung is beyond the scope of the current paper'. No stress statement.

sources.locator: handout p.5 ex.(19) and p.12 endnote 13 (to p.8 (33b) 'super-L tone > L tone')
sources.note: Morphosyntactic-diachronic study, not a tone description; NC !Xun and Ju|'hoan forms are cited with lexical tone marks (L, extra-L); Proto-Juu demonstratives reconstructed with the note 'tones are not reconstructed' (p.5 (19), endnote 8 on the tonal reconstruction of DIST *to'a); p.8 (33b) 'super-L tone > L tone' change explained by breathy-voice depressor loss; endnote 13 states the extra-L tone in Juu languages is frequently related to depressor consonants / breathy voice and pharyngealization and is 'not well documented yet'. No tone inventory, TBU or stress statement for NC !Xun.

From modern Khoisan languages to Proto-Khoisan: the value of intermediate reconstructions [От современных койсанских языков к пракойсанскому: значение промежуточных реконструкций]. sources.note: Proto-North-Khoisan (= Proto-Ju) step built on Snyman 1997's dialect survey incl. the North-Central lects Ok(ongo), Tsin(tsabis) and on Heikkinen 1986 Ov(amboland) !Xũ, i.e. kung1261 data among ~11 Ju lects. p.348 (p.12): 'tonal distinctions are not significant for the current article'. 'Tones' subsection of the Proto-Peripheral-Khoisan chapter, printed pp.430-431 (pp.94-95): 'it is reasonable to assume that PPeK was a tonal language - since all of its offspring have tonal systems'.. 'Out of all PeK languages, adequate description of the tonal system is only available for ǃXóõ and Zhu'hoan'..…
